name: whisper-large-v3-turbo-german (primeline)

lineage.how_derived: fine-tune of Whisper large-v3 for German, turbo variant (809M)

purpose: Whisper fine-tuned for German speech recognition: German transcription, voice commands, subtitling, search queries, dictation (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card metadata apache-2.0, no LICENSE file in the repo; canonical Apache-2.0 text read in https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-ASR/blob/main/LICENSE. Base model Whisper is MIT. Card disclaimer: a research model, not a commercial product of the publisher.

architecture.kind: AUTOREGRESSIVE encoder-decoder transformer (Whisper large-v3 turbo, 4-layer decoder)
architecture.why_this_design: Card: German fine-tune on a large mix of spoken German (flozi00/asr-german-mixed) to cut Whisper German errors.

benchmarks.name: German avg WER (Tuda-De, MLS, Common Voice 19)
benchmarks.harness: author eval set flozi00/asr-german-mixed-evals; whisper-large-v3-turbo 3.649, large-v3 3.279, CrisperWhisper 2.662

strengths: German-specific, Whisper tooling everywhere (AMD, Mac, CPU)
weaknesses: still a 30 s window Whisper: hallucination risk on silence (generic Whisper behaviour, not measured here)

tona_fit.reason: Easiest German upgrade over stock Whisper turbo (2.63 vs 3.65 on the author mix), Apache-2.0, 0.8B, every class and whisper.cpp-style engines. parakeet-primeline scores 2.95 on the same mix and is faster, but this one keeps Whisper tooling (timestamps, long-form chunking). Not on the independent leaderboard.

open_questions: Independent German WER (not on the Open ASR leaderboard)
Own long-form hallucination test on German audio with silence
